study_identification_part.si4_title: Dissimilarity in Sulcal Width Patterns in the Cortex can be Used to Identify Patients With Schizophrenia With Extreme Deficits in Cognitive Performance

cm1_research_objectives.reason: The paper clearly states its objectives: to extend PBSI to index individual similarity to healthy controls, apply a normative modeling approach on longitudinal MRI to quantify dissimilarity to the norm, and relate deviant PBSI-SW to cognition and sulcation. This covers explicit research questions and the purpose of applying normative modeling (identifying markedly deviating individuals and potential subgrouping/clinical relevance).
cm1_research_objectives.supporting_text: "We extended the PBSI such that it indexes the morphometric similarity of an independent individual (eg, a patient) with respect to healthy control subjects. By employing a normative modeling approach on longitudinal data, we determined an individual's degree of morphometric dissimilarity to the norm... A subgroup of patients with markedly deviant PBSI-SW showed extreme deficits in cognitive performance and cortical sulcation."

nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.reason: Eligibility criteria for healthy controls are described for both contributing cohorts, including exclusion of major medical/neurological illness and IQ < 80. Image quality and data completeness standards are specified via quantitative QA metrics and visual checks; explicit QA-based exclusions are reported. Final sample size for the reference cohort (164 controls; 328 scans at two time points) is provided along with overall scan exclusions from the initial pool.
nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.supporting_text: "Participants... included patients with schizophrenia and healthy controls... Participants with major medical or neurological illnesses or with an estimated IQ below 80 were excluded."; "After the evaluation of the computed quantitative measures of image quality, 138 scans were considered of insufficient quality and were excluded... In addition, 14 scans were excluded after this manual inspection."; "...resulting in 164 healthy participants and 164 patients, contributing a total of 656 scans."

nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.reason: Key covariates are incorporated: scanner and total brain volume are controlled in GAMMs, and PBSI-SW values are residualized for age, scanner, and total brain volume. Sex and age×sex were tested and dropped as non-significant. Multi-site/scanner effects are addressed by including scanner as a covariate (and testing scanner as random effect).
nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.supporting_text: "GAMM models were implemented... while controlling for scanner, total brain volume, and the random effect of the individual. We first fitted models, including a sex and age × sex term, but these terms were not significant."; "PBSI-SW values were residualized for age, scanner, and total brain volume..."

nm3_data_sources_reference_cohort.reason: The healthy reference cohort is drawn from two specified cohorts: the Utrecht Schizophrenia project and the GROUP consortium, with locations and recruitment context described.
nm3_data_sources_reference_cohort.supporting_text: "Participants for the current study were selected from a large longitudinal sample based on two cohorts... the Utrecht Schizophrenia project and the Genetic Risk and Outcome of Psychosis (GROUP) consortium, in Utrecht, the Netherlands."

nm4_image_acquisition_protocol.reason: Primary acquisition details are provided: modality (MRI, T1-weighted 3D fast-field echo), parameters (TE, TR, flip angle, FOV, voxel size, slices), and equipment (Philips Intera/Achieva 1.5T). Baseline and follow-up scans acquired on the same scanner for included participants.
nm4_image_acquisition_protocol.supporting_text: "Two scanners (same vendor, field strength and acquisition protocol) were used... Philips Intera or Achieva 1.5 T and a T1-weighted, 3-dimensional, fast-field echo scan with 160–180 1.2 mm contiguous coronal slices (TE 4.6 ms; TR 30 ms; flip angle 30°; FOV 256 mm; in-plane voxel size 1×1 mm²) ... All included participants had their baseline and follow-up scan on the same scanner."

nm5_data_preprocessing.reason: Preprocessing software and steps are specified: FreeSurfer v5.1 default pipeline for surfaces and volumes; BrainVISA v4.5 Morphologist for sulcal segmentation; detailed QA procedures including quantitative metrics and manual inspection are described.
nm5_data_preprocessing.supporting_text: "Images were analyzed using the FreeSurfer analysis suite (v5.1) with default settings..."; "For all images, sulcal segmentation and identification was performed with BrainVISA software (v4.5) using the Morphologist Toolbox..."; "we rigorously assessed the quality of the data using a combination of visual inspection and... QA metrics (SNR, CNR, FBER, percent artefact voxels, Entropy) ... ENIGMA criteria ... thresholds... and manual inspection."

nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.reason: The study constructs a normative reference from the healthy controls and applies Z-scoring to individuals; there is no description of data partitioning (e.g., hold-out or cross-validation) to validate the normative reference on unseen healthy data. The methods outline residualization and reference construction but do not mention internal validation splits.
nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.supporting_text: "We created a normative reference for PBSI-SW by calculating the average and standard deviation of the residualized PBSI-SW values for the healthy control subjects... Then, individual deviance... was calculated." (No mention of cross-validation/hold-out.)

nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.reason: There is no report of applying the normative reference to an independent external healthy dataset. Data sources are limited to the Utrecht and GROUP cohorts acquired at the same site.
nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.supporting_text: "Participants for the current study were selected from... the Utrecht Schizophrenia project and the GROUP consortium..." (No mention of external healthy dataset for validation).

nm8_normative_modeling_approach.reason: The statistical approach is described: compute PBSI across sulcal regions, residualize PBSI-SW for age, scanner, and TBV; build a normative reference from controls and compute Z-scores (PBSI-SW-Z) with |Z|>2 defining outliers; longitudinal effects assessed via generalized additive mixed models (GAMMs). Software environment R is reported.
nm8_normative_modeling_approach.supporting_text: "In a normative modeling approach, the deviation from the norm value... Here, we chose to apply normative modeling to a multivariate summary measure, PBSI. We extended the PBSI for patients such that it indexes the degree of similarity... to healthy control subjects."; "GAMM models were implemented... while controlling for scanner, total brain volume..."; "PBSI-SW values were residualized for age, scanner, and total brain volume..."; "We created a normative reference ... and ... calculated [PBSI-SW-Z]."; "All analyses were performed in R (https://cran.rstudio.com/)."

nm9_model_performance_reference_cohort.reason: The study does not report quantitative model fit or calibration metrics (e.g., explained variance, prediction error, coverage) for the normative reference among healthy controls. The methods detail residualization and Z-scoring but no performance metrics are provided for the reference model.
nm9_model_performance_reference_cohort.supporting_text: Methods describe constructing the control-based reference and computing Z-scores without reporting fit/calibration metrics for the healthy cohort.
nm9_model_performance_reference_cohort.location: Janssen2021.pdf.md: lines 98–114 (methods narrative; absence of performance metrics)

nm10_characteristics_reference_cohort_ea.reason: No internal data partitioning (e.g., train/validation/test or cross-validation) is performed for building/validating the reference; therefore, characteristics per partition are not applicable per the item’s NA condition.

nm11_reproducibility.reason: Software and versions are specified for preprocessing (FreeSurfer v5.1; BrainVISA v4.5) and the statistical environment (R). However, there is no statement about code, trained models, or data availability (open/restricted).
nm11_reproducibility.supporting_text: "Images were analyzed using the FreeSurfer analysis suite (v5.1)... For all images, sulcal segmentation... BrainVISA (v4.5)..."; "All analyses were performed in R..."

cr2_handling_of_clinical_covariates.reason: The study evaluates associations between deviation scores (PBSI-SW or outlier status) and clinical covariates such as PANSS change and medication (chlorpromazine equivalents), as well as cognitive measures (estimated IQ). These covariates are analyzed in relation to deviation, but not modeled as covariates in the primary normative deviation calculation.
cr2_handling_of_clinical_covariates.supporting_text: "...we compared ... PANSS total scores, positive, negative, and general subscores... estimated IQ... and sulcation index ... between the outlier and nonoutlier patient groups."; "Plots showing associations between PBSI-SW and chlorpromazine equivalents and change in PANSS scores... cr3_data_sources_clinical_cohort.reason: Clinical cohort MRI data sources are described as the Utrecht Schizophrenia project and the GROUP consortium, with recruitment setting and assessments detailed.

cr5_clinical_assessment_measures.reason: Clinical measures and assessment procedures are specified: diagnostic interviews (CASH/SCAN), PANSS for symptoms, and estimated IQ via WAIS-III subtests are described.
cr5_clinical_assessment_measures.supporting_text: "...CASH and ... SCAN... were used for diagnostic assessment..."; "Positive and Negative Symptom Scale (PANSS) ..."; "IQ was estimated from the performances on 4 subtests of the Wechsler Adult Intelligence Scale III..."

cr6_interpretation_of_deviation_scores.reason: Deviation scores are defined (PBSI-SW-Z relative to controls) and their interpretation is described (distance from normative value independent of age/scanner/TBV). A quantitative threshold (|Z| > 2) defines markedly deviant individuals (‘outliers’). Clinical implications are discussed: deviant patients show lower estimated IQ and decreased sulcation at follow-up; effect on trajectories is driven by deviants.
cr6_interpretation_of_deviation_scores.supporting_text: "...individual deviance ... was calculated [PBSI-SW-Z]... reflecting how deviant the PBSI-SW value ... is compared to the normative value ... independent of the participant's age, scanner, and total brain volume."; "Outliers were participants with |PBSI-SW-Z| > 2..."; "These patients had more severe deficits in estimated IQ and a lower sulcation index at follow-up... the effect of diagnosis on change of PBSI-SW over time was driven by the same small subset of deviating patients."
